characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: NOVEL MR5000 optical microscope at 200× magnification
characterization_methods.key_findings: M2-30 shows fine equiaxed grains with a high density of fine dark second-phase particles along grain boundaries and interiors (Fig. 1d).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Etched with 3 % FeCl3 + 10 % HCl (in ethanol) for 10–20 s; samples parallel to rolled surface; grain size measured per GB/T 6394-2002
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize phase morphology and grain size of M2-30

characterization_methods.key_findings: Random color distribution indicates no significant texture; M2-30 shows a unimodal grain-size distribution after aging (small grains grow slightly, large grains unchanged).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Mechanically ground and polished then electrochemically polished to strain-free surfaces; observation plane consistent with metallographic surface
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine grain orientation distribution and grain-size distribution of M2-30

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Thermo Fisher Scientific Apreo S LoVac
Thermo Fisher Scientific Talos F200X G2; Gatan precision ion polishing system for thinning
characterization_methods.key_findings: BF and SAED confirm two precipitate types ((Ti,V)C and κ) in M2-30; CDF images show κ-carbide number density and size increased versus 10 h aging with heterogeneous distribution, κ still predominantly precipitating at the edge of (Ti,V)C; HRTEM/FFT confirm intergrowth with (002)(Ti,V)C || (001)κ; ZA=[100] SAED with (020),(022),(002).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Samples ground to ~50 μm, 3 mm discs punched and ion-thinned to electron transparency
characterization_methods.purpose: Investigate morphology, chemical composition, dislocation configuration and crystal structure of precipitates in M2-30
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM): BF, DF/CDF imaging, SAED, HRTEM and FFT

characterization_methods.key_findings: V is obviously enriched at the (Ti,V)C carbides while Ti shows no enrichment; no Mn or Al enrichment determined at κ-carbides, indicating κ formation by composition ordering; carbon enriched at center of (Ti,V)C with a carbon-rich region surrounding it (Fig. 5).
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure carbon content at specific matrix positions and map elemental distribution around (Ti,V)C carbides
characterization_methods.technique: Electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) / EDS elemental mapping

characterization_methods.key_findings: M2-30 reached a yield strength of 884 MPa with only slight decrease in elongation; work-hardening rate maintained comparable to the solution-treated state, enhancing the tensile strength.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, strain rate 10^-3 s^-1, 2 mm thick × 58 mm long specimens along rolling direction, 12.5 mm extensometer, 0.2 % offset yield criterion
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the mechanical properties of M2-30

analytical_models.equation_role: Calculate stacking fault energy of the austenite matrix
analytical_models.model_note: Calculated SFE of M2 ≈ 78 mJ/m2, indicating dislocation slip as the deformation mode (Ti and V have little influence on SFE).

computational_details.simulation_method: Thermodynamic calculation of stacking fault energy (SFE) based on the Olson–Cohen thermodynamic model
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: SFE result (dislocation slip) is consistent with the planar slip deformation observed by TEM in M2-30.

analytical_models.model_note: σ0 matrix strength, σG grain-boundary, σD dislocation (neglected for both M1 and M2 after high-temperature solution treatment), σP precipitation strengthening.
r and f are the mean radius and volume fraction of κ-carbides.
Critical size of κ-carbides > 20 nm so shearing mechanism adopted.

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical yield-strength decomposition (matrix + grain-boundary + dislocation + precipitation strengthening)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated mechanism contributions sum to the measured yield strength (Fig. 10); for M2-30 the stack contains σ0 + σG + σOr + σS with the measured bar near the 900 MPa level.

analytical_models.model_note: Defines work-hardening stages; M2 shows Stage I (rapid slip) and Stage II (planar slip plateau), with M2-SS and M2-30 curves almost overlapping.

computational_details.simulation_method: Crussard–Jaoul analysis of the work-hardening index
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Work-hardening index curves of M2 before and after aging almost coincide, consistent with the preserved work-hardening rate and planar slip measured by TEM.

computational_details.simulation_method: Thermodynamic calculation of the phase composition
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Confirms that the matrix remains single-phase austenite after aging treatment, consistent with SAED observations.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Non-shearable (Ti,V)C carbides hinder dislocations (Fig. 12c); a region with higher dislocation density forms around them, increasing flow stress. Strengthening contributed by Orowan bypassing.

Highly coherent κ-carbides can be cut by dislocations, destroying coherence and causing glide-plane softening. In M2 the heterogeneous κ-carbide distribution combined with (Ti,V)C carbides does not soften the glide plane.

interfaces.interface_notes: EPMA mapping of M2-30 shows V is obviously enriched at (Ti,V)C carbides while Ti is not observed enriched; no Mn or Al enrichment is detected at κ-carbides, indicating κ-carbide formation by composition ordering rather than composition enrichment.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Before aging, pre-existing (Ti,V)C carbides are distributed in the matrix, surrounded by carbon-enriched zones. Upon aging at 550 °C, κ-carbides preferentially precipitate along the edge of (Ti,V)C carbides, utilizing these carbon-rich regions as precipitation sites.

phase_interfaces.coherence: intergrown; orientation relationship (002)(Ti,V)C || (001)κ confirmed by FFT
high coherence (much higher than (Ti,V)C/matrix); κ-carbides can be cut by dislocations

interfaces.slip_behavior: Both M1 and M2 deform by planar slip of dislocations (consistent with the high calculated SFE). The slip-band spacing of M2 is significantly smaller than that of M1, indicating more severe deformation and refinement of the dislocation configuration (higher work-hardening index).

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Tensile strength increased from 1004 MPa (Ti/V-free M1-30) to 1096 MPa (Ti/V-modified M2-30) while work-hardening rate is preserved; after aging, yield strength 884 MPa (M2-30) is comparable to 860 MPa (M1-30) despite reduced κ-carbide volume fraction; both steels exhibit planar slip with Ti/V-modified steel showing finer slip bands.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Material melted in a high-vacuum electric-arc melting furnace to produce the ingot of the Ti/V-modified low-density steel (M2).
Ingots hot rolled from 20 to 2 mm at 1000 °C followed by water quenching.
Samples solution-processed at 1000 °C for 30 min and water quenched; M2 in this state is named M2-SS. This is the parent process (proc_ss-1000c-30min).
Aging at 550 °C for 30 h followed by water quenching; M2 aged 30 h is named M2-30. This is proc_age-550c-30h.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Yield strength determined at 0.2 % offset; tested on an electronic universal testing machine (SUNS, UTM5105X)
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: 2 mm thick, 58 mm long; fabricated along the rolling direction; 12.5 mm extensometer

strain_hardening_rate: Work-hardening index curves of M2 before and after aging almost coincide; work-hardening rate preserved
tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–engineering strain curve and true stress–true strain/strain hardening rate curve (Fig. 7, legend M2-30 red solid curve)

stacking_fault_energy.note: SFE of M2 calculated via Olson–Cohen model; indicates dislocation slip as the deformation mode

defects.lattice_distortion: a region with higher dislocation density forms around the (Ti,V)C carbides (after deformation)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Unimodal distribution after 30 h aging (small grains grow slightly, large grains nearly unchanged); solution-treated M2-SS shows a bimodal distribution
grain_structure.texture: no significant texture in either state

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains with straight annealing twins
phases_present.texture: random color distribution indicating absence of significant texture

phases_present.crystal_structure: FCC (rock-salt type; (002) reflection indexed by FFT)
L-ordered (ordered domains; extra reflections in SAED)
phases_present.morphology: heterogeneous, clustered at the edge of (Ti,V)C carbides

precipitates.coherency: high coherence with the austenite matrix (shearable by dislocations)
precipitates.distribution: heterogeneous; preferentially precipitates at the edge of (Ti,V)C carbides, almost none in the matrix away from carbides
heterogeneously distributed, formed at high temperature and stable during aging

structures.overall_structure: Equiaxed austenite grains forming a single-phase austenite matrix after aging, with a heterogeneous (non-uniform) distribution of intragranular κ-carbides that preferentially nucleate at the edges of pre-existing high-temperature (Ti,V)C carbides. Grain size distribution becomes unimodal after 30 h aging. Thermodynamic calculations confirm the matrix remains single-phase austenite after aging.

unmapped_findings: For M2-30 the reported ultimate tensile strength is read from the abstract as 1096 MPa (vs 1004 MPa for the Ti/V-free M1-30) — the abstract states the Ti/V modification 'increases the tensile strength from 1004 MPa to 1096 MPa', which on the basis of the described comparison is interpreted as M1-30 → M2-30.

Yield-strength increase of ~200 MPa over M1 after solution treatment is attributed to (Ti,V)C precipitation (M2-SS), and after aging M2-30 reaches 884 MPa despite a reduced κ-carbide volume fraction, via dual Orowan bypassing of (Ti,V)C plus coherency strengthening of shearable κ-carbides.
The κ-carbide number density of ~7×10^22 m^-3 was reported only for M1-30 (Ti/V-free); no equivalent number density is given for M2-30.

Carbon-rich region around (Ti,V)C: carbon is enriched at the center of (Ti,V)C carbides and gradually decreases toward the edges, with a surrounding carbon-rich region exceeding the matrix carbon content; (Ti,V)C carbides act as carbon sinks reducing matrix carbon content.

Solution-treated M2 (M2-SS) contains intragranular (Ti,V)C carbides with an average size of 35.8 ± 20.1 nm and volume fraction 2.4 ± 1.4 %, which are pre-existing high-temperature precipitates that persist after 30 h aging (M2-30: 37.1 ± 22.6 nm, 2.3 ± 1.7 %).
